open_points.subject: disclosure-class ordering
open_points.text: “the members and the order have that one home [in `models`]” contradicts “`canonical_values` owns … The order of disclosure classes”
open_points.question: Which module owns the authoritative disclosure-class order, and does `canonical_values` merely apply that order or define it?
options: `models` owns the enumeration and order; `canonical_values` only computes comparisons and maxima
`canonical_values` owns the order and `models` only declares the members
open_points.default_guess: `models` owns the members and order; `canonical_values` implements comparison and highest-class operations from that enumeration.

open_points.subject: equal content submissions
open_points.text: “`canonical_values` owns A01 rules 1 and 4” assigns it rule 4, but rule 4 says an existing submission is returned unchanged, records nothing, and does not become current; `canonical_values` must not own storage, while `functions`, `flows`, and `store` are not assigned that rule explicitly.
open_points.question: Which module owns the record-aware behavior for resubmitting equal contracts, implementations, trial cases, flow versions, values, verdicts, and activations?
options: Each domain module owns the behavior for its records and uses `canonical_values` only for identity
`store` owns a generic atomic get-or-return-existing operation
`canonical_values` owns both identity and submission deduplication
open_points.default_guess: Each domain module owns the behavior for its records, using `canonical_values` to compute identity and `store` for atomic persistence.

open_points.subject: random entity identifiers
open_points.text: “`trial_execution_id`, `binding_id`, `run_id`, `approval_id` and `grant_id` are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.” State 3 assigns no module ownership for random generation or the collision check.
open_points.question: Which module mints and collision-checks random identifiers for M07, M11, M19, M24, and M25?
options: `store` atomically mints and checks every random record identifier
Each record-owning module generates identifiers and asks `store` to reject collisions
A separate lower-level identifier provider owns generation, with `store` checking uniqueness
open_points.default_guess: `store` atomically mints and collision-checks the identifiers because uniqueness depends on persisted records.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile writing responsibility
open_points.text: “Two [record types] have several [writing modules], on purpose: StoredValue M21 … and NodeExecution M23” conflicts with “`runs` … [sets the class] for function outputs, values and files alike” and “`effects` for service outputs, values and files alike”; the text also says a file is spooled before its record is written.
open_points.question: Is SpooledFile M22 a third multi-writer record, written by `runs` for function files and `effects` for service files, or does one module own creation of every M22 record?
options: Acknowledge M22 as a third multi-writer record with the stated provenance split
Make `store.spool_file` the sole creator of M22 records
Assign all M22 record creation to `runs` or to `effects`
open_points.default_guess: Treat M22 as a third multi-writer record: `runs` creates function-output records and `effects` creates service-output records, both through `store`.

open_points.subject: service error failure_detail and credentials
open_points.text: A17 says a resolved credential value “never enters … a failure detail,” while A09 says “The body of an error response is not interpreted; at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it is kept as `failure_detail`.” An untrusted service can echo the credential in that body.
open_points.question: How must `service_invoker` handle error-response bodies so the credential-exclusion invariant can be guaranteed?
options: Never persist error-response body content; retain only bounded transport/status metadata
Remove exact occurrences of the resolved credential before retaining the excerpt
Accept error-body excerpts and weaken the credential-exclusion invariant
open_points.default_guess: Do not persist error-response body content; keep only bounded status and transport metadata.
